analysis:
Examined all supplied documentation, patch and metadata units. docs/operations/provider-release.md:649–795 (head patch) introduces final-artifact runtime facts, catalog/CDN metadata fetching, optional release-carried cluster approvals, pair grants and public parity qualifications. It documents archive-hash checks, empty-environment CLI execution, signing-keychain removal, strict block/body limits, environment opt-in and coordinator rollout prerequisites. These are relevant to A-005, A-011, A-017, TB-011, T-054 and T-056; no executable evidence here establishes that these controls are bypassed or that cluster parity qualifications replace App Attest serving authorization. Existing trusted-writer and separate platform-ownership assumptions remain explicit at base lines 104–131.
Reviewed docs/developer/test.md:2308–2529, including cache preservation, media isolation, memory accounting, cancellation/retirement and build-scoped speed tests. These unchanged surrounding descriptions distinguish synthetic checks from physical-peer and installed-product qualification; they do not establish regressions in T-041, T-050, T-010 or A-018. The changed test-documentation orientation adds malformed-block, canonicalization and size-limit checks, but is not implementation proof.
Integration must examine scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh, scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-models.py, scripts/provider-release-publication.py, release workflows and ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts/ClusterPublicModels: verify metadata bounds and identity binding, secret isolation during artifact execution, and whether automatic grants/qualifications remain distinct from independently approved App Attest identity and current connection authorization. The linked platform parser/catalog/routing implementation was not supplied; verify its artifact binding, revocation and qualification-consumption contract without assuming a deployed version. The canonical model may need explicit coverage of release-derived pair/public qualifications after implementation review. No concrete regression is independently supported by this documentation-only source scope.
